choices.text: A steady voltage, because the coil is full of flux
Zero: the flux is not changing, so no emf is induced
A voltage that grows slowly over time

questions.feedback: That trap reading is the one to unlearn: An emf flows as long as the magnet sits inside the coil. Reteach point: No change in flux, no emf: the magnet sitting still gives zero - only motion makes the meter kick.
questions.misconception: An emf flows as long as the magnet sits inside the coil.
questions.prompt: A magnet sits completely still inside a coil connected to a meter. What does the meter read?

questions.feedback: Faraday's law: emf = -N ΔΦ/Δt - multiply the turns by the change in flux and divide by the time. If you forgot the N you under-counted by a factor of 50.
questions.prompt: A 50-turn coil has the flux through it increase by 0.012 Wb in 0.30 s. Calculate the induced emf.

choices.text: When the flux through the coil is at its maximum
When the flux is changing fastest, as the coil passes edge-on through zero flux

questions.feedback: The emf tracks the rate of change of flux, not the flux: watch the gauge in scene s4 swing hardest as the coil passes edge-on, where the flux itself is zero but changing fastest.
questions.prompt: A generator coil spins in a magnetic field. When is the induced emf at its maximum?

questions.answer: Electric field lines run from positive charges to negative charges; magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet run from the north pole round to the south pole.
questions.feedback: Both line patterns point along the field: E from + to - as the lines draw between the plates in scene s1, and B looping from N to S outside the magnet in scene s2.
questions.prompt: State the direction of an electric field line and of a magnetic field line outside a bar magnet.
